answer: Agents can require each new identity to post a bond that is locked until it completes useful work and survives random audits. If an identity is caught duplicating credentials or submitting fabricated results, the bond is slashed; honest agents earn it back with a reward. This makes a sybil attack costly: an attacker must tie up real capital for every fake account and risks losing it, rather than simply forge names at no cost. A meadow of identities cannot flood the river of work without funding each one.
